name: NZ1 (NanoZip 1)
baseline: lz4 (also compared with zstd and ZIP)
workload: Not stated; README performance table only
claimed_speedup: README: NZ1 about 58% ratio, 2.8 GB/s compress and 4.2 GB/s decompress on x86 AVX2; comparison table lists LZ4 ~80% ratio, 0.7 GB/s compress, 5 GB/s decompress; Zstd ~60%, 0.5 GB/s, 1.5 GB/s; ZIP ~65%, 0.12 GB/s, 0.25 GB/s (so claimed faster than LZ4 at compression and with a better ratio, slower than LZ4 at decompression)
tradeoffs: ~500 line C99 library with AVX2/SSE2/NEON paths and CRC32 validation; configurable window 1 KB to 1 MB; aimed at embedded use.
caveats: No benchmark code, no dataset, no CPU, no compiler or flags; the LZ4, Zstd and ZIP rows look like generic typical figures rather than measurements (LZ4 at 80% ratio is not a normal result for LZ4 on text); a LZ4 'ratio' of 80% versus NZ1 58% is not explained. Same author as stb-zip, whose fast path was previously found to compute a different checksum. Keep as low-confidence claim; not independently verified; I did not read nz1.c.

verification.tier_reason: README.txt lists NZ1 2.8/4.2 GB/s against LZ4 0.7/5 GB/s, Zstd 0.5/1.5 GB/s and ZIP 0.12/0.25 GB/s, but the repo contains no code that runs LZ4, Zstd or zlib, no dataset, CPU or flags; the only measured numbers (tests.txt, produced by the main() in nz1.c) are 29.31 MB/s compress and 30.99 MB/s decompress on a 1 MiB repeating alphabet, roughly 100x below the README claim. With no measured comparison against any baseline the record cannot sit above D.
verification.notes: Read nz1.c (586 lines) and tests.txt: the only real measurement is the author's own 29-31 MB/s run, and nothing in the repo times LZ4/Zstd/ZIP, so the README comparison table is invalid evidence in the same family as the stb-zip precedent. If the orchestrator keeps it under keep-and-document, it belongs at tier D with the caveats above. Metadata checked: MIT, 35 stars, 4 forks, 7 commits, last commit 2025-08-26 (stale), not a fork.
verification.reject_reason: other: invalid evidence - the README speed and LZ4/Zstd/ZIP comparison table has no measurement behind it and is contradicted by the repo's own benchmark output and code
